info.text:
Claiming Social Security at 62 can shrink your check 30%, usually for good.
Born 1960 or later? Full retirement age is 67. Claiming at 62 pays 70% of the full benefit; waiting to 70 pays 124% (SSA rules).
Our math: a $2,000 check at 67 is $1,400 at 62 or $2,480 at 70.
The cut usually sticks (rare exceptions: withdrawing within 12 months or suspending at full retirement age), but COLAs still apply: the 2027 COLA is 3.6% (SSA, Oct 14, 2026).
Our math: break-even for 62 vs 67 is around age 79.
Sources: Social Security Administration; CNBC (Oct 14, 2026).
News and education, not financial advice.
